messages.author: b742296e4d6ce88e
messages.subject: Intercepts in a Multigroups hierarchical CFA model
parts:
Hi everybody,
I am not familiar with multigroup analysis but I have tried to do a Multigroups hierarchical CFA model and I get in trouble in estimating intercepts:

Here is the syntax:   

# I combined the covariance matrices, sample sizes, and means into single list objects
combined.cov <- list(sld=sldCov, norm=normCov)
combined.n <- list(sld=905, norm=2200)
combined.means <- list(sld=sldMeans, norm=normMeans)

############################
#Lavaan Models
############################

#Wisc-IV classical structure with 4 factors
wiscClass <-
'
#model matrix
PRI =~ 1*DC + CI + RM
VCI =~ 1*SO + VC + CO
WMI =~ 1*MC + LN
PSI =~ 1*CR + RS
#structure matrix
g =~ 1*PRI + VCI + WMI + PSI
PRI =~ 0 * VCI
PRI =~ 0 * WMI
PRI =~ 0 * PSI
VCI =~ 0 * WMI
VCI =~ 0 * PSI
WMI =~ 0 * PSI

'

# models
strong.fit6 <- sem(wiscClass, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n,  sample.mean=combined.means, group.equal=c("intercepts"))
# Or
strong.fit6 <- sem(wiscClass, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n,  sample.mean=combined.means, group.equal=c("loadings","lv.variances","lv.covariances","residuals","intercepts"))

#Here is the error
In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!


# I did not have problems with the following models
#structure invariance
strong.fit2 <- sem(wiscClass, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n,  sample.mean=combined.means)
#construct-level metric invariance or equal factor loadings
strong.fit3 <- sem(wiscClass, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n,  sample.mean=combined.means, group.equal=c("loadings"))
#variance and covariance
strong.fit4 <- sem(wiscClass, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n,  sample.mean=combined.means, group.equal=c("loadings","lv.variances","lv.covariances"))
#residuals
strong.fit5 <- sem(wiscClass, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n,  sample.mean=combined.means, group.equal=c("loadings","lv.variances","lv.covariances","residuals"))

Can anybody help? Is there any error in my syntax or in the specification of the model?

Thanks a lot,
David

messages.subject: Re: Intercepts in a Multigroups hierarchical CFA model

#Wisc-IV classical structure with 4 factors
wiscClass <-
'
#model matrix
PRI =~ 1*DC + CI + RM
VCI =~ 1*SO + VC + CO
WMI =~ 1*MC + LN
PSI =~ 1*CR + RS
#structure matrix
g =~ 1*PRI + VCI + WMI + PSI
PRI =~ 0 * VCI
PRI =~ 0 * WMI
PRI =~ 0 * PSI
VCI =~ 0 * WMI
VCI =~ 0 * PSI
WMI =~ 0 * PSI

'

Those last lines of syntax are unnecessary and might inadvertently be doing something unintended (like creating unintended phantom variables).  Also, the fixed first factor loadings are redundant with lavaan's defaults.  Do you still get errors after running the script below?

wiscClass <- '
# first-order factors
PRI =~ DC + CI + RM
VCI =~ SO + VC + CO
WMI =~ MC + LN
PSI =~ CR + RS 
# second-order factor
g =~ PRI + VCI + WMI + PSI
'

It might also help to post your versions of lavaan and R:

sessionInfo()

Terry

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Intercepts in a Multigroups hierarchical CFA model
parts: How can I impose equality constrain in syntax without using the "group.equal"  function?
# second-order factor

g =~ PRI + VCI + WMI + PSI
'

You can use labels to constrain parameters.  Any parameters with the same label will have the same value.  There are several examples of fixing parameters to specific values or setting free parameters to equality across groups on the lavaan web site:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html

You will only be able to test invariance of higher-order "measurement" parameters for the lower-order factors whose measurement parameters are invariant across groups.  

Terry

messages.author: cf3b2060e1fe46a5
messages.subject: Re: Intercepts in a Multigroups hierarchical CFA model
parts:
I'm currently doing a multigroup cfa of a bifactor model with 65 items and 14 specific factors. I'm running a configural invariance model, then I'm constraining the model through the group.equal argument, including loadings (metric invariance) and then loadings and intercepts together (scalar invariance).

I noticed that when loadings are constrained, the degrees of freedom increase by 115, which makes sense: 51 df for the specific factors and 64 df for the general factor.

However, when intercepts are also constrained for scalar invariance, the degrees of freedom increase only by 50 in total. I would have expected an increase of 115 df. This makes me wonder if some of the intercepts are not being constrained. 

I only get this type of issue when testing hierarchical models (e.g. bifactor and higher-order). For simple (lower-order) models, the degrees of freedom gained are the same with metric and scalar invariance.

Any thoughts?

Thank you for all your work.

Ylenio

messages.subject: Re: Intercepts in a Multigroups hierarchical CFA model
parts:
On 12/02/2015 10:09 PM, yleni...@gmail.com wrote:
> Thank you for your reply.
>
> I had a look. Basically, for scalar invariance, 65 equality constraints
> have been added for all the intercepts. However, the model only gained
> 50 degrees of freedom. Does the fact that there are 15 overall factors,
> with one marker variable each, make up for the difference?

No. What also happens (and it is easily missed) is that -once you
constrain both factor loadings and intercepts- lavaan will (by default)
estimate the means/intercepts of the latent variables. All except those
from the first (baseline) group.

Yves.
